g.title: PS1
g.text: Mobile power source; output voltage and loaded behavior require validation.

g.title: W_P6_PI_HEADER
g.text: Four owned Elegoo/Dupont jumper leads - P6 Pi power
Use two positive and two return leads of equal short length, at most about 12 inches. Cut/strip the DROK ends and use the correct mating ends at H1; reject on heat or voltage drop.

g.title: H1
g.text: 23 mm GPIO extension; four used contacts shown
One header exposes these contacts through the M.2 HAT+ stack. Confirm actual fit, pin numbering, and jumper gender before power.

g.title: PI1
g.text: Logical USB labels identify device assignments; mark the selected physical sockets during assembly.

g.title: CBL_P7_DUE_USB
g.text: P7 data-capable USB-A to micro-B cable
Internal colors are diagram conventions, not field-wiring instructions.

g.title: CBL_HUB_UPSTREAM
g.text: Integral to the owned hub; measure the actual revision's lead length before mounting.

g.title: CBL_COOLER
g.text: Keep the keyed plug and captive lead intact.

g.title: CBL_PCIE
g.text: Keep the managed high-speed cable intact and verify connector orientation before latching.

g.title: CBL_CAMERA
g.text: Standard-to-Mini FFC, 22-pin Pi end to 15-pin camera end
Use the owned unequal-ended cable; the Pi end is 22-pin / 0.5 mm and the camera end is 15-pin / 1 mm. Verify orientation before insertion.

g.title: CBL_LIDAR_USB
g.text: Internal colors are logical conventions; use the development kit cable and adapter intact.

g.title: PSU1
g.text: Official Raspberry Pi 27 W USB-C power supply
Bench-only alternative to the DROK header feed.

g.title: CBL_P0_USBC
g.text: Logical power representation of the complete USB-C cable; do not field-wire it.

g.title: DUE1
g.text: This link supplies Due power and carries bidirectional serial data.

g.title: HUB1
g.text: Owned Adafruit #2998 USB Mini Hub with Power Switch
Bus-powered 4-port USB 2.0 hub with captive USB-A upstream lead
The single switch controls all four downstream ports. Leave the external-power jack unused because it is tied directly to USB 5 V and can back-feed the Pi. The hub adds ports, not power budget.

g.title: A954
g.text: Active USB-to-UART conversion occurs inside this cable; USB and TTL signals are not direct nets.

g.title: W_BNO_TTL
g.text: Connect the individual female sockets to the BNO055 soldered male header.

g.title: BNO1
g.text: One owned female-to-female Elegoo/Dupont jumper from 3VO to PS1 selects UART mode; PS0 remains at its default LOW state. Do not connect a STEMMA QT cable while UART mode is selected.

g.title: COOL1
g.text: Supplied four-wire fan plug and lead
Use the cooler's supplied lead intact; a STEMMA QT cable is not a substitute even though both use small four-pin shells.

g.title: HAT1
g.text: This already-operating assembly is shown as managed connectors, not field-wired individual conductors.

g.title: CBL_M2
g.text: Seat and retain the SSD according to the HAT instructions.

g.title: CAM1
g.text: The FFC is treated as an indivisible assembly, not as field-wired conductors.

g.title: LIDAR1
g.text: Future connection; add only after the Pi 5 A source and USB budget are validated.
